I farm the way I have learned over many years: I do not chase the highest possible yield if it means more risk, more labor, or more cash tied up in the field. I have 14.5 mu under a wheat-maize rotation, and with only two people in the household, I will keep the whole area in the same system because it matches my land, my irrigation, and the way I already work. Since I have well irrigation, I will use that to protect the crop at the key stages instead of watering too often. For wheat, I will plant an improved variety, not an old local seed, because I want steadier yield and better stand, but I will keep fertilizer at a moderate level so the crop does not lodge and so I do not waste money. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage on this size of land and fits the wheat-maize rotation well. I will irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat in my area depends more on timely water for overwintering, jointing, and grain filling. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what gives me the most reliable return in summer. I will keep fertilizer balanced but not excessive, give fewer irrigations than wheat, and use fewer pesticide sprays unless pressure becomes obvious. I am managing for stable production, manageable labor, and lower risk across the whole year.
